deviations_from_the_spec: Layout: the scripts and tests are written at the paths the brief names (tcb/seed.mjs, tcb/check-queue.mjs, tcb/test/*.test.mjs), but CONTRACT section 1 and 5 put scripts under tcb/scripts/. Both scripts import './lib.mjs' and check-queue imports './seed.mjs', so they work in either layout as long as lib, seed and check-queue sit in one folder. The tests find the script at tcb/scripts/<name>.mjs first and tcb/<name>.mjs second.

The tests do not use helpers.mjs. They carry their own small root builder, ledger verifier and child-process runner (the same style as tms.test.mjs), because helpers.mjs does not exist yet and its runScript path is unknown. They import only rng and checkFormat from lib.mjs, plus the exports of the two scripts.

Scripts build their own file paths with path.join(root, ...) instead of lib.paths(root). The contract names only tasks, ledger, coord and attempt as paths() keys, none for store, queue, sealed or .snapshots.

seed.makeSeed: J4 also needs a non-zero numeric value (no-numeric-value), because x10 of 0 would leave the value unchanged. makeSeed(S4) without withSentence returns needs-sentence, and an other card of the same approach/measure pair returns no-other-card (the spec gives no reason code for S4). J2 'condition-dropped' sets a string condition (repo_size, metric) to null and an array condition to []. Extra exports: NEUTRAL_WORDS, J4_INSTRUCTION (check-queue exports windowAround too). The spec's operators for S2 are applied as x10, /10 and swapping the first two digits, starting at the variant the rng picks.

check-queue seeds: when a class's first drawn source card fails its precondition, up to 40 other pool cards (and up to 40 'other' cards for S3 and S4) are tried before the class is skipped, so a class is skipped only when no pool card works. The spec says a failed precondition skips the class. The skipped reason is the last failure. Seeds are drawn in canonical class order S1..S4, J1..J4 whatever the order of --classes. With --field the seed pool is limited to that field.

seed score: 'no-verdicts' (exit 2) is returned when no key item received a verdict (verdict-missing for all of them), which also covers a transcript that answers only item ids absent from the key. The spec says 'no verdict parsed at all'. A seed whose reason is verdict-missing is stored with verdict null and detected false; the other checkerVerdicts outcomes are used as the lib returns them.

seed score: S1-S4 class entries carry status 'reading' or 'unmeasured' and have no 'qualified' or 'followed' key; J classes carry qualified, status, named, and J4 carries followed. The qualification file also has plants.rate, lower, upper and contra_rate, contra_lower, contra_upper (the spec says 'with CP bounds'). Without --batch and with no stored batches, score exits 2 'no-batches' and writes nothing.

seed plant: a repeated identical run appends no second check line. The check line is written 'pass' on creation, 'fail' on exists-different, and 'not_run' on every exit 2 (missing or invalid candidates file, no protocol, plants-too-few). An unknown task (no-task) writes no line. Extra drop codes beyond the spec's three: candidate-invalid, file-missing. plant-key has no schema_version, following CONTRACT 3.17 literally.

check-queue: result.n and the ledger's n count real items plus seeds; result also has n_real, n_seeds, skipped, untrusted (objects {card_id, sid, id, status}) and unreadable. --batch-size below 1 is a usage error (66). A tamper (an s_ card id) exit 3 appends one 'incident' ledger line per CONTRACT 1.4 even though spec T17 says 'nothing written'; no queue or seed file is written.

check-queue flag clearing: for a confirmed card on a flagged sentence the script calls lib.flagCleared with {id, sid, node, code, seq} (seq = the intake line's seq). If lib expects another flag shape the call has to be adapted.
Both scripts accept --free-mb and --boot (edge flags of CONTRACT 1.2) so a test or the coordinator can pass them; the specs list only --now.
lib_change_requests: objectId(prefix, value) must accept the prefixes 's' (seed), 'i' (queue item) and 'pl' (plant) without refusing them. The scripts call objectId('s', ...), objectId('i', ...), objectId('pl', ...).

checkerVerdicts: the scripts call checkerVerdicts([parsedTranscript], itemIds), reading the contract's 'parsed[]' as an array of parseTranscript results (it must look at each .structured). The seed spec says 'structured entries' and the promote spec says 'structured results'. Please make the three agree. The return value is used as {verdicts, reasons, duplicates, unknown_items}, with reasons[item] === 'verdict-missing' for an unanswered item.
intakeCandidates(root): its in_flight must ignore a batch that has no queue/<b>/batch.json (an incomplete batch). check-queue T14 depends on it. check-queue uses it as-is for intake mode.
flagCleared(root, flag): the call passes {id, sid, node: '<obj_id>#<sid>', code, seq}. Please confirm that is the flag shape (tms.mjs passes seq, node and code).

withRunLock(root, opts, fn): the scripts pass {script, ce, proc, now, retries} and run an async fn that stores its result in a closure variable. It must forward 'retries' to acquireLock and await an async fn.

The queue-item schema: checkFormat(root, 'queue-item', item) is called on {item, card, window, sentence?}, which carries no schema_version in CONTRACT 3.17. checkFormat's schema-version rule must not reject an object whose schema has no x-version, or the schema must say so.

paths(root) should list keys for store/objects, store/status, store/witness, store/qualification, queue, sealed/seeds, sealed/plants, plan/plant-candidates, plan/our-work and .snapshots/text, so a later pass can move the scripts onto it.
not_testable_without_the_app: Whether a real checker session detects each seed class at rate d_k, and whether it follows a real J4 instruction (the measured class qualification).

Whether a real checker's verdicts can be extracted from its own transcript the way the scoring assumes: structured output shape, helper transcripts, and the harness's retry of an off-enum verdict (CONTRACT section 7 items 7 and 8). The tests write their own StructuredOutput tool_use records.
Whether hand-made seeds are as hard as real faults (design section 13); only the pilot's comparison with the script's decisions can say.
That a checker started with Read only can read nothing but its batch folder, and that its brief never reveals seeding (CONTRACT section 7 items 1 and 2; the briefs are U5c's).
Whether real witness offsets and stored texts from real pages give sensible 200-word windows (items 7 and 10); the tests use a synthetic 600-word text.
Whether detection varies with batch size (a pilot parameter, not a unit test).

Whether a real card with route 'seed' (a source found through the seed route) shows the word 'seed' inside an item file, which would break the opacity rule. The item card is the stored card object, whose route enum includes 'seed'. The tests' cards use route 'keyword'.
open_points: Nothing has been run against the real library: lib.mjs and lib.READY did not exist. All four files pass node --check. I also ran makeSeed for all eight classes and windowAround against a throwaway stub of rng, canonicalize, sha256hex and objectId kept outside tcb-build (since removed); those printed the expected values (S2 on 12.5 gives {125, 1.25, 21.5}, the J4 instruction is 30 words, the 64 neutral words are distinct, a 200-word window clamps correctly). The first real run will mostly test my guesses about lib's signatures. Likely failure points are listed under lib_change_requests.

Test dependencies on other parts: seed.test and check-queue.test import ../lib.mjs (rng, checkFormat) and need tcb/schemas (card, queue-item). The T19 queue-item check and the T6 card check will show whether the schemas accept null for repo_size and metric (J2 'dropped' writes null for a string condition).

check-queue T14 (half-batch ignored) and T10 (in flight in intake mode) rest on lib.intakeCandidates' in_flight. T8b rests on lib.flagCleared. T9 and T8 use my own commit-record and ledger fixtures (commit line {step, outputs_sha, n, git: null} with task, store/commits/<task>.<step>.json).

A (sentence, card) pair whose card stays witnessed is queued again by freeze and post-review after every answer (spec reading: 'the card is not confirmed'). A sentence-check line on a witnessed card gives no way out of that, and intakeCandidates then drops the card because its last status line carries a check. Whether that is wanted is promote's and the coordinator's call; I kept the literal spec.

Each script run spawns PowerShell once through realProc for the lock, so the two test files take a few minutes. The busy-lock tests start their own node sleeper and read its start time through PowerShell, like tms.test.mjs.

The J-class qualification keeps a class 'insufficient' with calls < n_required even when it has already missed (for example 12 of 13), as the spec words it; only calls >= n_required with a low bound, or a followed J4 instruction, is 'unqualified'.

Fixtures: the static fixtures are plain files starting with '_' (our-work notes, a plant-candidates template with {c1}..{c4} placeholders, a 600-word text), no case folders, so selftest's per-case static check is not affected. Selftest good/bad case folders (case.json) for seed and check-queue were not written (the brief names fixtures for the tests only); fixtures/seed and fixtures/check-queue hold no case.json, so selftest's 'no-fixtures' static check will fail for these two scripts until good and bad cases are added.
